menu.hint: A short game with a guide: every basic action in one turn

ui.loading: The Stranger is setting the table for you…
ui.doThis: Complete the highlighted action on the board

steps.intro:
Take a seat. I'll show you the basic moves, then you can try things for yourself.

I've done the work, made deals and messed up other people's plans. If something helps me win, I'll use it.

Your goal is to score the most points in 15 rounds. They come from businesses, projects, your role (+3 while you hold it) and bonus points — from lobbying, for example. Money and influence will help you get there. Let's begin.
steps.work: Let's start with something simple. Press “City job” on the right to earn 2$. Not much, but sometimes that's all you're short of.
steps.workDone: There's your first payment. Remember, you usually have three actions per turn. A job helps when you're just short of a purchase, but it won't carry you through the whole game.
steps.campaign: Now let me show you how to get your first influence. Press “Exchange” and trade 5$ for 3◆. It'll come in handy when money alone isn't enough.
steps.buyObject:
Buy the “Corner Pharmacies” on the market. They'll pay income every round. At the end of the game, a business also earns points equal to half its price, rounded down.

Medicine for the city, income for us.
steps.role:
Now let's take a role. Each one here has its own opportunities.

Open “Roles” on the right and take the Journalist. Its bonus and special power apply while you hold it. Let's try blowing up a story.
steps.power:
Victor is in our way. He already has four scandals. Add a fifth and he'll lose the Capitalist role.

Press “Blow up a story” and choose Victor. I'd offer him a deal first, but this is cheaper.
steps.scandals:
Victor lost his role. But that story gave you a scandal too.

• Each scandal left at the end costs you 1 point.
• Most roles are lost at five scandals. Your Journalist's threshold is six.
• Exceed the threshold and you're arrested: your turn ends at once if it's yours, you get just one action next turn, your scandals drop to zero, and you lose your role and one Protection.
• Crisis PR and some role powers can reduce scandals.
• Without a role, one scandal fades at the end of each round.

Once you lose the Journalist, the normal threshold applies again. Watch that counter.
steps.cards:
I've got something else lined up. Our rivals don't need to know everything we're planning.

Press “+ Draw 2 cards” above the end-turn button. Two action cards cost one action, 4$ and 1◆.
steps.playCard: That'll come in handy. Play “All Hands” from your hand to gain one action. Playing the card doesn't spend an action itself.
steps.charity:
There's time for a good deed too. Take the “Charity Fund”: it has no special requirements, so you only need to pay its cost.

The city gets help, you get points.
steps.terminal:
Now I want the “River Port”, but it requires a logistics business. The “Smuggling Terminal” will do. Buy it on the market.

Yes, smuggling. I'm not passing up a profitable purchase over its name.
steps.port: That gives us access to the port. Take the “River Port” project before someone else does. We can leave the terminal's origins out of the opening speech.
steps.grey:
The terminal belongs to the Grey Sector and unlocks shady deals. Find them on the right and run “Dirty rumours” against your rivals.

The result depends on the die. I've arranged a good roll for this tutorial. At a regular table, you'll have to take your chances.
steps.greyDone:
It worked. A bad roll could have left you with scandals instead.

There's another obstacle: Protection blocks “Dirty rumours” and other shady attacks on its owner without being spent. We have a special move for that — “Break Protection”.
steps.roof: Victor is unlikely to let this go. Buy Protection: right now it costs 3$ and one action. The price rises in later rounds. I wouldn't skimp on security.
steps.roofInfo:
You have Protection. Here's what you can count on.

• It blocks shady attacks on you and stays in place. “Break Protection” is the exception.
• It absorbs one hostile card or role power, then is spent. Special moves that remove Protection bypass this rule.
• A protected role cannot be bought out.
• You can usually hold one Protection; the Mobster can hold two.
• “Slip Past the Guards”, “Poach the Guards” and the Enforcer's “Take Protection” can also remove it.

And remember: guards won't save you from scandals caused by your own actions.
steps.lobbying:
Back to negotiations. You have influence; time to get something tangible out of it.

Press “Lobbying”: spend 10◆ to gain 6 points. Influence left over at the end earns no points.
steps.endTurn:
That's it for now. You normally have three actions per turn; I gave you more for the lesson. Now they're gone.

End your turn. Let's see what the others have done.
steps.roundEnd:
A new round has begun. “Your turn — what changed” collects the events since your last turn.

Your businesses paid income. The three oldest market cards were replaced, and one project went to the bottom of its deck. That's why you shouldn't put off a purchase too long.

The player with the lowest score acts first. Everyone tied for last gains 1◆. Now let's check the chronicle.
steps.revenge:
As expected: Victor played “Dirt File” against you. Find the entry in the chronicle — Protection took the hit and was spent.

It would have stayed after “Dirty rumours”, but a card is different. You'll need to hire security again before your next dispute.
steps.finale:
That's the basics covered. Try it yourself now. If we end up at the same table, I'll be playing to win too.

A few things to remember:
• Take suitable projects while they're available.
• Turn money and influence into points before the game ends.
• Watch your scandals and your role's threshold.

Don't stick to just one approach. See what works best right now.
steps.cardsMobile:
I've got something else lined up. Our rivals don't need to know everything we're planning.

Open your Hand at the bottom and press “+ Draw 2 cards”. Two action cards cost one action, 4$ and 1◆.
steps.playCardMobile: That'll come in handy. Play “All Hands” from your Hand to gain one action. Playing the card doesn't spend an action itself.
steps.city: The business you bought is now in your city. Open the “My city” tab at the top — it shows all your businesses, their income and your free slots.
steps.cityDone: There are your “Corner Pharmacies”. You can switch between the “Projects”, “Market” and “My city” tabs at any time — one at a time, so the cards are easy to read.
steps.terminalMobile:
Now I want the “River Port”, but it requires a logistics business. Go to the “Market” tab and buy a business with the “Logistics” tag — the “Smuggling Terminal” will do.

Yes, smuggling. I'm not passing up a profitable purchase over its name.
